hook.text: Processing speed peaks at twenty-five and slowly declines. But vocabulary keeps growing until seventy.

buildup.text: Fluid intelligence (raw problem solving) fades with age. Crystallized intelligence (knowledge) does not.

discovery.text: Older adults struggle with new tech but excel at judgment calls. Experience compensates for speed.

twist.text: Cognitive reserve—built through education, exercise, and social ties—can delay decline by years.

climax.text: The aging brain isn't just losing power. It's reorganizing—recruiting new regions to stay effective.

punchline.text: Older brains aren't weaker. They're different.

quiz.question: What type of intelligence keeps growing into old age?
